py.name: Python
py.tutorNote: Python runs inside the app (Pyodide): input() works; there is no window for graphics (no turtle, tkinter or pygame).

js.name: JavaScript
js.tutorNote: JavaScript here runs on Node, not in a browser: console.log prints to the output panel; prompt("question") shows the question and returns the line typed in the input box, and alert() prints its message. No document, window or other page APIs — for those, use an .html file.

css.name: CSS
css.runNote: CSS styles a web page rather than running on its own. Put it in a <style> block inside an .html file (or link it from one), and Run will show the styled page.

ts.name: TypeScript
ts.tutorNote: TypeScript here is type-checked first; type errors stop the run with the line and column. It runs on Node: console.log prints to the output panel, prompt("question") returns the line typed in the input box, alert() prints its message; no document or window.

json.name: JSON
json.tutorNote: A .json file is data, not a program. Run checks that it's valid JSON: it prints "Valid JSON." or the first mistake with its line and column. Rules: keys in double quotes; commas go between items in objects and arrays; no comma after the last item in either; no comments.

md.name: Markdown
md.runNote: Markdown is text to read, not a program to run.

c.name: C
c.tutorNote: C here is compiled by Clang to WebAssembly: standard input and output work; no graphics or OS-specific headers (windows.h, conio.h). It enforces C99 and later: write int main(void) and #include the header for every function used (stdio.h for printf and puts).

cpp.name: C++
cpp.tutorNote: C++ here is compiled by Clang to WebAssembly without exceptions: try/catch and throw don't compile; iostream, string, vector and map work; no graphics.

bas.name: BASIC
bas.tutorNote: BASIC here is qbjc, a QBasic/QuickBASIC-compatible interpreter with text output only: no graphics statements (SCREEN, PSET, LINE as graphics, CIRCLE, PAINT, DRAW) and no `?` shortcut for PRINT. It is QBasic, not QB64 or FreeBASIC: a FUNCTION's type comes from a suffix on its name (FUNCTION Add% (a%, b%)) or none at all — `FUNCTION Add (a AS INTEGER, b AS INTEGER) AS INTEGER` doesn't parse here.
